# Requirements Document — Honest source annotations in generated artifacts

**Document Version:** 1.0
**Date:** 2026-08-12
**Author:** Generated by the shape skill
**Stakeholders:** Kit maintainer (owner); every downstream reader of a generated artifact, human or agent
**Status:** approved (2026-08-12)
**Decomposition:** populated (2026-08-12)
**Entry point:** discover
**Profile:** software (of config: software)
**Notes:** UX ideation skipped: not UI-facing (`ui_facing: false` in config)

> The Status, Decomposition, and Notes lines are the document's own progress record —
> the shape skill's resume derives position from them. Keep them current.

**Reading the tier codes used below.** Generated artifacts label each line with where its
content came from: `1-code` (read from this repository), `1-docs` (fetched official
documentation), `2-context7` (a community-maintained source), `1-profile` (the kit's own
delivery-profile methodology), and `3-model` (model knowledge, no external source). Only
the first four can point at something a reader could go and check; `3-model` cannot,
which is why the two are treated differently throughout this document.

---

## 1. Business Objectives

- **Primary goal of this feature:**
  Make every generated artifact's source annotation state only what the kit can actually
  back, so that a reader who did not run setup can tell grounded lines from ungrounded
  ones without leaving the file.

- **Key business outcomes / KPIs this drives:**
  - Zero occurrences of `verified:` in newly generated artifacts — the field asserts a
    standing verification the kit has never performed and cannot perform.
  - 100% annotation coverage on kit-written lines, so that an unannotated line signals
    human authorship rather than an emitter that forgot.
  - `schema_version` read by at least one consumer, closing a field currently written by
    every artifact and consumed by nothing.
  - A dated audit of maintainer-controlled repositories returns a non-zero count of
    demoted or deleted lines, or returns zero and thereby answers whether the annotation
    prompts any action at all.

- **Alignment to company priorities:**
  This is a correctness fix to the kit's central claim. The kit's argument for adoption is
  that its records are trustworthy — plans, gates, findings, conventions. An artifact
  asserting verification it does not have discredits every annotation the kit writes, not
  only the stale one. [ASSUMPTION: no formal OKR structure exists for this project; the
  objective is the kit's own credibility.]

---

## 2. Problem Statement / User Needs

- **Current pain points / inefficiencies:**

  Setup writes convention and rubric files annotated with a source and a `verified:` date.
  Nothing re-checks whether that source still resolves or still supports the claim, and one
  source URL was already dead the day it was written — a 404 shipped into a generated
  artifact and caught only by chance.

  The rules themselves usually stay correct, which is what makes this hard to see: the
  failure is not wrong reviews, it is that the record lies about *why* a rule is trusted.
  It never announces itself and surfaces only after a rule that quietly stopped being
  grounded has been enforced for months.

  Three specific defects, each confirmed by direct inspection of artifacts generated on
  2026-08-12:

  1. `gates.md` stamps `tier: 3-model · verified: 2026-08-12` on coverage thresholds that
     were never verified against any source — the kit asserting verification of its own
     invented defaults.
  2. The kit ships unannotated lines of its own (the Linear Conventions skeleton bullets),
     so absence of an annotation cannot currently distinguish a human-written line from a
     kit-written one.
  3. `schema_version` is written into every artifact and read by no script or hook, while
     the adjacent `provenanceMatches()` function proves the technique works offline.

  The load is asymmetric by construction: these files are written once per project and read
  on every skill run afterward, so the read count grows without bound while the
  verification count stays at one. The only existing mitigation — setup's re-run offering
  re-verification past six months — fires on stack change rather than on a schedule, so
  artifacts rot fastest in the repositories whose code moves least, and it never forces, so
  it is declined by whoever is in a hurry.

- **Who is impacted:**
  - **The agent reading the artifact (primary).** It treats `verified:` as a fact and
    reviews work against a rule whose grounding evaporated. It never follows the link, so
    it has no path to noticing. This is the worse case and the one the design must serve.
  - **The person reading the artifact (secondary).** At least capable of noticing a dead
    link on clicking it.
  - **Someone inheriting a repository (most acute).** They read the conventions as the
    team's decisions, cannot distinguish a line grounded in a live source from one grounded
    in a 404, and cannot ask whoever ran setup because that person has moved on. Every line
    reads equally authoritative.

- **Evidence supporting the need:**
  The three confirmed defects above, verified by direct file inspection. Separately, a
  vendor rename — Databricks changing Asset Bundles to Declarative Automation Bundles in
  March 2026 — produced shipped content naming a product that no longer existed. That
  incident motivated an open work row proposing a freshness clock; the clock was never
  built. [ASSUMPTION: no telemetry exists on how often readers act on annotations —
  Objective 4's audit is designed to produce that evidence.]

---

## 3. Scope

**In Scope:**

- Replacing `verified:` with `read_on:`, a field that records a read event rather than
  asserting a verification state.
- A distinct `ungrounded` token for lines that never had an external source
  (`3-model` conventions, scaffold-default thresholds), replacing the date entirely.
- A distinct `unreachable:` token for a source that was fetched and did not resolve,
  keeping it separable from a source that never existed.
- Annotation coverage on every line the kit writes, so that an unannotated line signals
  human authorship.
- Stating what an annotation promises, the editor's obligation, and the admission that
  human authorship is heuristic — in the artifact's own legend, readable without kit
  internals.
- A stated rule for a verification run record, defined without emitting an empty one.
- Bumping `schema_version` and adding a consumer that reads it.
- Suppressing source annotations for fetches that did not resolve, and surfacing those
  failures to whoever is running setup.
- A tier-aware conversion of existing artifacts, proposed through setup's existing
  diff-and-propose path, never applied automatically.
- One clause in the shared skill contract so that a finding citing an artifact line states
  when its source was read rather than implying currency.

**Out of Scope (for this phase):**

- **The mechanical classifier.** No subcommand that parses annotations and reports or fails
  on their state. Deferred deliberately, pending evidence that readers act on the
  annotation at all.
- **Source snapshotting.** No archived copy of what a source said when a line was written,
  and **no reserved field for one** — an unfilled field would be the kit asserting
  structure it is not backing.
- **Any automated fetching, re-dating, or scheduled job.**
- **Any change to the setup preflight gate's verdict vocabulary, to `path-guard.js`, or to
  CI.** Routing a freshness verdict into either enforcement path converts a trust problem
  into an outage.
- **Detecting content drift** — a source that still resolves but no longer supports the
  claim. See Section 10; this is a named limitation, not an oversight.

---

## 4. Units of Work / Scenarios

- **Unit 1 (Urgent): Define the annotation grammar.** A reader can look up exactly what
  every annotation state means — grounded, never-grounded, unreachable, and absent — and
  what an annotation promises, without network access or knowledge of the kit's internals.
  This is the foundation the other units emit and read.

- **Unit 2 (Urgent): Emit the new grammar when setup writes artifacts.** A project set up
  after this ships gets artifacts whose every kit-written line carries an annotation that
  states only what setup actually did — a read, a failed fetch, or no source at all.

- **Unit 3 (High): Read the schema version at the gate.** A reader or agent encountering an
  artifact written under an older grammar learns that fact instead of silently misreading
  it under current rules.

- **Unit 4 (Medium): Convert existing artifacts on a setup re-run.** A project set up
  before this ships can bring its artifacts onto the new grammar without anyone hand-editing
  them and without any date being refreshed.

- **Unit 5 (Medium): Cite grounding honestly in review findings.** An agent citing a
  convention or rubric line in a finding states when that line's source was last read,
  rather than presenting it as currently verified.

**High-level flow — the inheritor's journey, which is the case this feature exists for:**

1. Someone inherits a repository they did not set up and opens `conventions.md`.
2. They read the file's legend, which states what an annotation promises and admits which
   distinctions are heuristic.
3. They scan the lines: `read_on:` lines point at a source someone read on a stated date;
   `ungrounded` lines never had one; `unreachable:` lines had a source that did not resolve
   on a stated date; unannotated lines were written by a person.
4. They form their own judgment about whether a date is old enough to matter — the file
   states no policy and asserts no expiry.
5. For any line they distrust, they re-read the source and update the date, delete the line,
   or demote it to `ungrounded`.

All of this happens offline, inside one file, with no knowledge of the kit's source catalog.

---

## 5. Functional Requirements

| Requirement ID | Description | Priority | Acceptance Criteria |
|---|---|---|---|
| FR-001 | The annotation grammar defines `read_on:` as the field recording that a source was read on a date | Urgent | - `artifact-schemas.md` §1 defines the field and its date format<br>- The definition states it records an event, not a standing verification<br>- It applies to `1-code`, `1-docs`, `2-context7`, and `1-profile` tiers |
| FR-002 | The grammar defines `ungrounded` as the token for lines that never had an external source | Urgent | - Defined for `3-model` lines and scaffold-default thresholds<br>- Carries no date<br>- Grammar states that a date on such a line would assert a read that never happened |
| FR-003 | The grammar defines `unreachable:` as the token for a source that was fetched and did not resolve | Urgent | - Records the date of the attempt<br>- Grammar states it is distinct from both a successful read and from `ungrounded`<br>- A reader can tell "we tried and failed on this date" from "there was never a source" |
| FR-004 | The grammar states that an unannotated line signals human authorship | Urgent | - Rule stated in `artifact-schemas.md`<br>- Accompanied by the explicit admission that this is heuristic, not guaranteed<br>- Names the two ways it breaks: pre-existing files, and an emitter that omits an annotation |
| FR-005 | The artifact's own legend states what an annotation promises and the editor's obligation | Urgent | - Legend states the annotation claims someone read this source on this date **and that the line follows from it**<br>- Legend states that editing an annotated line's text obliges the editor to update or drop its annotation<br>- Legend is readable with no network, no source catalog, and no knowledge of kit internals |
| FR-006 | The grammar states the rule for a verification run record without emitting an empty one | Urgent | - Rule states that a pass writes an itemised dated record when it runs<br>- Rule states that absence of a record means no pass has ever run<br>- Record distinguishes checked, unreachable, and never-grounded<br>- No empty record is emitted by any current code path |
| FR-007 | The shared skill contract requires a finding citing an artifact line to state when its source was read | Urgent | - Clause added to `artifact-schemas.md` §8<br>- Clause states the finding must not present the line as currently verified |
| FR-008 | Setup emits `read_on:` for every successfully read source | Urgent | - Applies across conventions, gates, and rubrics<br>- Date is the date of the read |
| FR-009 | Setup emits no source annotation for a fetch that did not resolve, and records `unreachable:` instead | Urgent | - A non-200 response produces `unreachable:` with the attempt date, never a `read_on:`<br>- Setup retries once before recording it<br>- Setup tells the operator, at run time, which sources did not resolve |
| FR-010 | Every line setup writes carries an annotation | Urgent | - Includes the Linear Conventions skeleton bullets that currently ship bare<br>- Verifiable by grep: no kit-written line lacks an annotation |
| FR-011 | Artifacts carry a bumped `schema_version` reflecting the new grammar | High | - conventions and gates move 1 → 2; rubrics moves 2 → 3<br>- Value written into frontmatter on generation |
| FR-012 | A consumer reads `schema_version` and reports when an artifact predates the current grammar | High | - Implemented in `scripts/setup-runtime.js`<br>- Follows the offline single-line-match pattern already used by `provenanceMatches()`<br>- Reports the mismatch; **does not** change the preflight gate's blocking verdict |
| FR-013 | A setup re-run proposes a tier-aware conversion of artifacts written under the old grammar | Medium | - `1-code` / `1-docs` / `2-context7` / `1-profile`: `verified: <date>` → `read_on: <date>`, same date preserved<br>- `3-model` and scaffold defaults: `verified: <date>` → `ungrounded`, date dropped<br>- Runs only through setup's existing diff-and-propose path; never automatic<br>- No date is ever moved forward |
| FR-014 | Review skills state grounding age when citing an artifact line | Medium | - Applies to critique, verify, fix, and tidy<br>- A finding citing a line reports when its source was read<br>- A finding citing an `ungrounded` or `unreachable:` line says so |
| FR-015 | The verb change is validated against an agent reader before the grammar is committed | High | - Two versions of the same conventions file, one using `verified:` and one using `read_on:`<br>- A model is asked to classify each line's grounding<br>- Result recorded; if the model does not distinguish them, the field name is reconsidered before FR-001 is merged |

Priority distribution: 10 Urgent, 3 High, 2 Medium. This exceeds the 60% guideline for
Urgent+High and is flagged deliberately rather than adjusted — see Section 10, Open
Questions, Q1. The unit-level distribution (2 Urgent, 1 High, 2 Medium) sits at the
guideline, and the unit is the level at which work is scheduled.

## 6. UI/UX Requirements

Not applicable — `ui_facing: false` in `.ai-delivery/config.md`. This feature has no
screens, components, or user interactions. Its entire interface is the text of a markdown
file read by a person or an agent, and the requirements governing that text are FR-004,
FR-005, and FR-006 in Section 5.

The one presentation decision worth recording: the annotation must remain readable inline
within a bulleted markdown line, since that is where it lives today and changing the
carrier would break the "existing files stay readable" constraint.

---

## 7. Non-Functional Requirements

- **Portability:** Anything executable is a Node script under the kit's shared runtime. No
  shell commands, no shell syntax, no assumption about which shell exists. The kit is
  proven on macOS and untested on Windows and Linux, and Windows is where shell assumptions
  break first. A solution requiring a shell does not ship.

- **Offline operation:** Every annotation state must be interpretable with no network
  access. Fetching belongs only in an explicitly human-triggered pass — never in a hook,
  never in a routine skill run, never in CI, because none of those is guaranteed to have
  network or to be run at all.

- **No central state:** These artifacts live in other people's repositories, committed to
  their git history, touched only when a skill runs. There is no registry, no database, and
  no kit-side record of what was verified when. Whatever the mechanism knows must be inside
  the artifact. This rules out any service-shaped design.

- **Backward readability:** An artifact written under the old grammar must never become
  unparseable or silently misread. It need not remain valid, but it must declare which
  grammar produced it.

- **Hand-edit survivability:** User edits to these files are treated as team decisions. The
  mechanism must survive a human rewriting a line, deleting an annotation, or adding a
  convention with no annotation at all. It cannot assume the kit wrote everything it reads.

- **Interpretability without internals:** A reader must not need the kit's source catalog,
  network access, or knowledge of how the kit works to understand what a line's annotation
  is telling them.

- **Security:** No new outbound network path is introduced in this phase. The one existing
  fetch path (setup's research phase) gains a failure-recording behaviour but no new
  capability. FR-009's operator message must not embed content derived from a fetch
  response, since artifact text is read as authoritative by every later agent run.

- **Data / integrations:** No external services. No new dependencies. The change is
  confined to the kit's own specification files, the setup skill, one Node script, and four
  review skills.

---

## 8. Design System & Implementation Notes

Not applicable — `design_system: null` and `ui_facing: false` in
`.ai-delivery/config.md`. No component library is involved.

The equivalent constraint for this feature is the **annotation grammar itself**, which
plays the role a design system would: it is the shared vocabulary every artifact and every
consuming skill must use identically. Its canonical definition lives in
`skills/setup/references/artifact-schemas.md` §1, and no skill may define a variant of it
locally.

**Files expected to change:**

| Area | File | Nature of change |
|---|---|---|
| Grammar definition | `skills/setup/references/artifact-schemas.md` | §1 annotation grammar; §3/§4/§5 skeletons; §8 contract clause |
| Authoring behaviour | `skills/setup/SKILL.md` | Research and generation phases; re-run and staleness table |
| Version consumer | `scripts/setup-runtime.js` | New reader following the `provenanceMatches()` pattern |
| Finding citation | `skills/critique/SKILL.md`, `skills/verify/SKILL.md`, `skills/fix/SKILL.md`, `skills/tidy/SKILL.md` | Citation clause copied from §8 |

**Custom needs:** None. The `unreachable:` and `ungrounded` tokens are new vocabulary but
are defined in the same grammar file as the existing tiers.

## 9. Success Metrics & Acceptance

- **How we will measure success:**
  - **Primary test.** A person who did not run setup sorts every line in `conventions.md`
    and `gates.md` into grounded, ungrounded, and human-authored — offline, without leaving
    the file. The first two hold by construction; the third is heuristic and the file says
    so. If this does not hold, nothing shipped that matters.
  - Zero occurrences of `verified:` in newly generated artifacts, and every kit-written
    line annotated. Both halves checkable by grep.
  - `schema_version` read by at least one consumer.
  - **Dated audit.** Six months after the grammar ships, hand-audit the
    maintainer-controlled repositories and count lines that were demoted or deleted versus
    re-dated. A non-zero demote-or-delete count indicates readers are acting; zero indicates
    the annotation alone does not prompt action, which is the evidence that the deferred
    classifier is needed. [The six-month interval is the proposed default and is the
    maintainer's to confirm — see Section 10, Q2.]

- **Definition of Done:**

  | Stage | Done When |
  |---|---|
  | Requirements | All 10 sections complete; approved by the kit maintainer |
  | UX Ideation | Not applicable — not UI-facing |
  | Validation gate | FR-015 has run and its result is recorded. The grammar is not merged until a model has been shown both versions and its ability to distinguish them is known |
  | Implementation | FR-001 through FR-014 met; no `verified:` in generated output; every kit-written line annotated; `schema_version` read |
  | Release | Plugin version bumped so installs actually receive the change — a content-only commit reports "already at the latest version," which is a false success |
  | Measurement | The audit date is recorded at release time and the audit is performed on it |

---

## 10. Risks / Dependencies / Assumptions / Open Questions

**Risks** — carried from the discovery risk pass, which was one independent perspective
rather than complete coverage. The full inventory is at `risk-challenge.md`.

- **The deferral has no instrument.** The decision to build the classifier was deferred
  pending evidence, and the no-central-state constraint makes cross-install evidence
  uncollectable. *Mitigation:* the dated self-audit in Section 9 is the named trigger, with
  the maintainer as owner. It sees only maintainer-controlled repositories, which is a
  stated limitation of the evidence rather than a gap in the plan.
- **The absence-means-human rule is unenforced and breaks on invited hand-editing.** A
  person who rewrites an annotated line's text while leaving the annotation attached
  produces a line whose annotation vouches for wording the source never contained — the
  original failure re-created inside the new grammar. *Mitigation:* FR-005 states the
  editor's obligation and admits the distinction is heuristic. Nothing detects a violation;
  this is accepted, not solved.
- **The verb change is an untested bet on how a model reads metadata.** *Mitigation:*
  FR-015 is a merge gate, not a follow-up.
- **Transient fetch failures could mislabel lines permanently.** A rate-limit during one
  setup run could leave lines looking ungrounded forever. *Mitigation:* FR-009's
  `unreachable:` token keeps the states separable, plus one retry and an operator message.
- **The change ships but is not installed.** A content-only commit to a local marketplace
  reports "already at the latest version." *Mitigation:* the plugin version bump is a
  named Definition-of-Done stage.
- **Priority inflation.** Ten of fifteen functional requirements are Urgent. *Mitigation:*
  flagged as Q1 below rather than silently adjusted.

**Dependencies:**

- Unit 1 (the grammar) must land before Units 2 and 5, which emit and cite what it defines.
- Unit 4 (migration) must land after Unit 2, because both modify `skills/setup/SKILL.md`.
- Unit 3 (the version consumer) depends only on the version numbers agreed at
  decomposition, not on the grammar text, so it can proceed alongside Unit 1.
- No external teams, services, or APIs.

**Assumptions:**

- **[ASSUMPTION] Content drift, not link rot, is the dominant real-world failure.** This is
  a stated position, not a measured finding. Its consequence is named plainly: **nothing in
  this phase, and nothing in the deferred classifier, detects a source that still resolves
  but no longer supports the claim.** Both address the minority case. This is the single
  most important caveat in this document and is deliberately not buried — a reader
  evaluating whether this work was worth doing needs it.
- **[ASSUMPTION] Converting `verified:` to `read_on:` at the same date is honest.** The
  reasoning: a line the kit verified on a date was necessarily read on that date, so the
  conversion strictly weakens the claim while preserving the date, and therefore does not
  constitute refreshing a date without a re-check. This holds for every tier except
  `3-model`, where the original `verified:` recorded a read that never happened — which is
  why FR-013 converts those to `ungrounded` instead.
- **[ASSUMPTION] No telemetry will ever be available.** The audit is a hand count on
  repositories the maintainer controls.

**Open Questions / Decisions Needed:**

| # | Question | Owner | Target Date | Decision |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Q1 | Ten of fifteen functional requirements are Urgent, against a 60% guideline. Is that honest for a small tightly-coupled change where each piece is load-bearing, or should some drop to High? | Kit maintainer | Before decomposition | Pending |
| Q2 | Is six months the right interval for the audit that triggers the classifier decision? | Kit maintainer | At release | Pending |

Five open questions carried from discovery were resolved during intake and are recorded
here as closed: the field name is `read_on`; old files get a tier-aware conversion proposed
by a setup re-run; a failed fetch records `unreachable:` and is distinguishable from a
source that never existed; the citation clause lands in five files rather than every skill,
confirmed by inspection; and content drift is stated as the real failure mode above.
